Pontiac, IL 61764

Courthouse was built in 1875 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. J.C. Cochrane designed the historic edifice of the County's third Court

brief: Second Empire county courthouse of 1875: red brick with white stone quoins and trim, corner pavilions with mansard roofs, a tall central clock tower with a mansard-and-cupola top, and a columned entrance porch. Stands in the middle of the courthouse square with a Civil War monument on the lawn. Record: 3 Commons photos plus 14 HABS measured drawing sheets.

facade.notes: the Livingston County Courthouse (Pontiac IL, 1875): a red-brick Second Empire courthouse with white stone quoins and arched window hoods, mansard corner pavilions, a central clock tower with a lantern, a columned entry porch; on a courthouse square with clipped hedges and big trees

why.note: a civic building is a raised, symmetric block set apart by steps, lawn and a portico
the courthouse-square town: the courthouse in the middle of its own block, a tower visible from every street into the square
